newsitem.title: USA: Loctite agrees to merge with Henkel.
newsitem.headline: Loctite agrees to merge with Henkel.

text.p: Germany's Henkel KGaA and Loctite Corp. said Thursday they agreed to a merger in which Henkel will acquire the 65 percent of Loctite it does not already own for about $1.3 billion, or $61 in cash per share.
The agreement, unanimously approved by Loctite's board, comes five weeks after Henkel first unveiled a proposal to buy Loctite for $56 a share.
Early in November, Henkel raised its bid to $57.75 a share, and late Wednesday raised it again to $61, conditioning the transaction on a deal acceptable to both sides.

"Henkel's increased offer represents excellent value for our shareholders," said Robert Fiondella, chairman of the Loctite special board committee set up to weigh offers for the adhesives and speciality chemical company.
"The proposal comes at the end of a process designed to produce the best transaction," he said.

Last week, Hartford, Conn.-based Loctite effectively opened the door to all potential bidders by establishing a formal auction process to sell itself. Under that process, Loctite set a deadline of Wednesday afternoon for offers from interested parties.
Based on Loctite's 32 million shares outstanding, the Henkel merger offer is worth about $1.27 billion.
Loctite, which also makes sealants and coatings, earned $84 million, or $2.40 a share, on revenues of $785 million last year.
One of the conditions that Loctite had required was that its Hartford office remain open for at least two years.

"We see a continuing role of importance for the management and employees of Loctite in the ongoing, combined business," said Dieter Winkhaus, chief executive of Dusseldorf-based Henkel. "Moreover, we expect the Hartford office to remain an important centre for the operation of our combined adhesives business going forward.

"We anticipate that the (Hartford) office will be maintained for an even longer period," Winkhaus said in a letter to the Loctite committee that was included in Henkel's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on its increased offer.
Loctite's stock gained 37.5 cents to $60.75 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
